extraction.Name: Bennett Sierra
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want his patent in fee to his 160 acre allotment, for he did not want to pay taxes, but he got a letter from Pine Ridge Agency, telling him to come and get his patent, and, as he understood that the allotment would be charged up with taxes, for which it would finally be sold, he accepted the patent
extraction.Buyer: Mortgaged to A. Barker, of Denby, South Dakota, for $150.00; sold to Joe Harris, of Denby, South Dakota, for $800.00 over and above the mortgage, this $800.00 being taken out in trade—horses and cattle
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: as he understood that the allotment would be charged up with taxes, for which it would finally be sold, he accepted the patent
extraction.Occupation/Income: farms his wife's allotment and trucks freight for the United States Government
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent, has poor health, stomach trouble; has a wife and three children to support; family has good health except one boy; mortgage was not satisfied before sale in 1921; deponent considers he received a very poor price for his land; has never received any aid from the County, State nor the United States Government; document dated December 1, 1928
